beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:wonder, setting the scene]From space, the Sahara has an ^eye. [act:measured, letting it grow][tune:fall]^Forty kilometres across: a long day's ^walk from one rim to the other. [act:quiet, a little eerie][tune:fall]Ring inside ring, staring straight ^up.
[d:tension][act:reporting the claim, even]^Millions of people online say it's ^Atlantis, the lost city of legend. [act:brisk, rolling up sleeves][tune:fall]Let's ^look.

[d:calm][act:storytelling, plain]The legend comes from ^Plato, a philosopher of ancient Greece. [p:0.93][act:storytelling, painting it]He described Atlantis as rings: two of ^land, three of ^water, around an ^island, like a target set in the ^sea. [act:adding detail, unhurried][tune:level]Beyond the Pillars of ^Heracles, the old name for the strait of ^Gibraltar. [go:1|0][act:placing it, gently final][tune:fall]Facing the ^Atlantic.

[d:build][act:turning to it, curious][tune:rise]And the ^Eye? [act:ticking them off][tune:level]^Rings? [act:a quick nod][tune:fall]Yes. [act:next one][tune:level]Near the ^Atlantic? [act:a quick nod][tune:fall]Yes. [act:and one more][tune:level]Mountains to the ^north, the ^Atlas. [sfx:shimmer][act:generous, warm][tune:fall]It's a ^good match. [gap:0.4][act:the small catch, dry][tune:fallrise]At ^first.

[d:build][act:inviting, hands on the table][tune:fall]Now put them side by ^side, drawn to the same scale. [act:measured, precise][tune:level]Plato's city: about ^five kilometres across. [sfx:hit][act:the punch, blunt][tune:highfall]The Eye: ^forty.

[d:build][go:3|0][act:plain, a little amused][tune:fall]It's ^eight times too big. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Line up eight of Plato's cities, edge to edge, and they only just reach across the ^Eye. [act:adding the second strike][tune:fall]And it sits ^high in the desert@noun, hundreds of kilometres from ^any sea. [act:dry, a smile][tune:fall]A strange spot for an ^island.

[d:build][act:explaining, clear and patient]Cut it open, and the rings are ^layers of rock. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Picture a stack of blankets, pushed up from below into a ^dome. [act:explaining, clear and patient]Then the ^wind@air shaves the top off, flat. [act:the payoff, delighted]Each layer's cut edge shows as a ^ring, the hard ones standing up as ridges. [act:a quiet aside of wonder][tune:fall]And they carry on ^underground.

[d:aside][act:curious, light][tune:rise]How ^old are they? [p:0.9][act:light, wide-eyed][tune:fall]These rocks formed between about a ^thousand and four hundred and fifty ^million years ago. [act:tossed off, then a grin][tune:fall]Older than the ^dinosaurs, by a few hundred million years.

[d:reveal][act:the second surprise, lean in][tune:fall]And it isn't a ^crater, either: no rock from space dug this ^bowl. [sfx:shimmer][act:telling the real story, steady]^Molten rock pushed the dome up from ^below. [act:telling the real story, steady]Hot ^water, rising through it, ate out the ^centre. [act:the last step, unhurried]Then, over millions of years, ^wind@air did the carving. [d:build][act:summing up, affectionate][tune:fall]A natural ^blister, sanded ^down.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]Atlantis in the ^Eye? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]*Ruled ^out*. [act:turning to the open door, warmer][tune:rise]But people living here long ago, when the Sahara was ^green, with lakes and grassland? [act:honest, gently hopeful][tune:fall]^Possible, and ^barely surveyed.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:a concession, sincere][tune:fall]The Eye is ^real, and it is ^spectacular. [gap:0.45][act:the last word, quiet][tune:fall]The ^city in it ^isn't.
